links.comparator_used: Original, unsimplified Chinese TMD patient education materials (Group A)
links.effect: Mean sentence length 21.1 vs 33.9 characters (p < 0.001); actionability 95.6% vs 16.7% (p < 0.001)
links.tradeoff: LLM-only rewrites were less accurate than clinician rewrites (clinician accuracy 4.48 vs 3.23). Limited depth on TCM concepts. Actionability attenuated under a concise prompt.
links.quote: LLM-rewritten texts demonstrated significantly shorter sentences (21.1 vs. 33.9 characters, p < 0.001) and substantially higher actionability (95.6% vs. 16.7%, p < 0.001) compared with original texts.

links.comparator_used: LLM-rewritten texts released without clinician review (Group B), with clinician-only rewriting (Group C) as a second reference
links.outcome: Accuracy and actionability of patient education materials, plus clinician time
links.effect: Human-AI collaboration accuracy 4.49, matching clinician accuracy of 4.48 (p = 1.000) and above the 3.23 reported for the lower-accuracy comparison. Actionability preserved at 95.6%. Clinician time reduced by 72%.
links.tradeoff: Clinician review time is still required, though 72% less than clinician rewriting. LLMs showed limited TCM conceptual depth, which expert oversight is meant to address.
links.quote: The human-AI collaboration model matched clinician accuracy (4.49, p = 1.000) while preserving LLM actionability (95.6%), with 72% less clinician time.

design_hint: human-AI collaboration / clinician review of outputs
